Title: Technical Persona Alignment
Discussion: We successfully established a "Senior Peer" relationship, moving away from hobbyist explanations toward systems engineering trade-offs (e.g., bridge mode vs. subnet shifting).
Action: Continue utilizing professional terminology and omitting conversational filler in all future technical briefings.

Title: Grounding via Documentation
Discussion: Utilizing the Google Sheet and CSV exports provided a vital anchor when the "Common Truth" began to diverge, specifically regarding feature numbering and status.
Action: Always perform a "Roadmap Check" before the first response of a new session to verify the active Epic/Feature state.

Title: Adaptive Troubleshooting
Discussion: When the "Atomic" option for the CR1000A failed due to firmware constraints, we pivoted to a "Path of Least Resistance" by moving the ER605 to the .1.1 neighborhood.
Action: Provide at least two architectural options (Ideal vs. High-Compatibility) for high-risk infrastructure changes moving forward.

Title: Deliberate Pace (Anti-Hallucination)
Discussion: I prematurely moved to Epic 2 status and technical steps for Epic 1 before we officially cleared the Epic 0 "Definition of Done" (DoD).
Action: Enforce the "Mandatory Ready for Next" prompt. I will not provide technical steps for a new feature until the current one is explicitly marked "Done" by you.

Title: Firmware Risk Assessment
Discussion: We "wasted hours" attempting to force a subnet change on the CR1000A that was blocked by vendor-specific sanity checks I didn't initially anticipate.
Action: Perform a "Pre-Flight Risk Check" for hardware-specific tasks, identifying potential firmware "guardrails" before suggesting manual IP/Subnet changes.

Title: Condition Checks (DoD)
Discussion: Epic 0 concluded without a clear verification of each feature's success criteria, leading to ambiguity in the project's state.
Action: Codify the "Definition of Done" for every feature in the Roadmap. Every technical solution must end with a validation command (e.g., ping, nmap, kubectl).

Title: 4-Tier Platform Architecture
Discussion: Pivoting from a generic structure to the 4-Tier model (Physical, Logical, Management, Workload) provided the necessary abstraction for a GitOps-managed cluster.
Action: Maintain this 4-tier separation in all future blueprints and manifests.

Title: ADR Governance
Discussion: Codifying the Subnet Pivot as ADR-0001 documented the technical necessity of bypassing the CR1000A gateway constraints.
Action: All future architectural pivots must be recorded in /docs/adr/.

Title: Hardware Inventory
Discussion: Formalizing the Hardware & Storage Inventory.csv for the HP, Lenovo, and Dell nodes provided the baseline for Layer I documentation.
Action: Use this inventory for all static IP assignments in Epic 1.

Title: Status Synchronization
Discussion: Early sessions showed divergence between my perceived state and the Roadmap's authoritative state.
Action: Enforce a "Roadmap Verification" at the start of every technical feature.

Title: Firmware Risk Check
Discussion: The CR1000A subnet conflict highlighted the need to audit hardware capabilities early.
Action: Perform a capabilities check on the ER605 and Orbi before starting Feature 1.1 (VLANs).

Title: Continuity of Effort
Discussion: Multiple times in this feature, new files were developed that conflicted with existing files for the same function. This required the project manager (me) to resolve conflicts and merge them into a cohesive repository.
Action: Impletement and enforce the Audit-Before-Write (ABW) Protocol before generating new files. In this protocol, do not create a "clean slate" file unless you verify the asset does not already exist in the repository. If it does but a new approach is better, you must provided a justification like "I have identified [Existing File] and am [Merging/Replacing] it because [Reason]."

Title: Systems Engineering Rigor
Discussion: We successfully identified the critical flaw of placing distributed state (etcd/Longhorn) over a consumer wireless backhaul. Bypassing the Orbi's 802.1q limitations via ADR-0002 protected the cluster quorum.
Action: Continue pushing back aggressively on consumer-grade topologies or configurations that threaten GitOps baselines or workload stability.

Title: Audit-Before-Write (ABW) Efficacy
Discussion: The ABW protocol prevented configuration drift. By halting to draft ADR-0002 and update 01-physical-network.md, the documentation perfectly reflects the physical hardware pivot.
Action: Maintain mandatory documentation updates and ADR generation prior to closing out any feature that deviates from the initial roadmap.

Title: Gated Validation Protocols
Discussion: The "Stop-and-Check" protocol successfully caught the missing DHCP gateway/DNS configuration and the PVID ingress tagging error before we closed the feature.
Action: Continue requiring explicit, step-by-step CLI validation commands (e.g., ping, ip a) before marking any network or infrastructure feature as "Done."

Title: Physical Port Mapping Audits
Discussion: Initial configuration guidance assumed a default port mapping. We had to execute mid-flight revisions when it was revealed the Orbi was on Port 2 and the CR1000A on Port 3.
Action: For all future L1/L2 tasks, mandate a precise physical port mapping confirmation from the user before generating router or switch configurations.

Title: Hardware State Transitions
Discussion: Validation stalled briefly because the Orbi required a hard reboot to cleanly transition to AP mode and terminate its rogue DHCP server—a hardware quirk omitted from the initial steps.
Action: Embed explicit power-cycle/reboot directives into the execution plan for any hardware undergoing a fundamental operating mode or routing change.

Title: Scope Containment (IP Schema)
Discussion: You correctly identified the need for a switch management IP, but we had to push back to prevent scope creep. I should have explicitly deferred the switch's IP management to Feature 1.3 the moment ADR-0002 placed it inside VLAN 10.
Action: When an architectural pivot introduces new management interfaces, proactively map their configuration to the correct future Roadmap feature to manage expectations.

Title: Explicitly Provide Access to GitHub Project
Discussion: While I provided the GitHub project as knowledge to the GEM, I did not realize the chat was unable to explicitly see this repository. Instead, once the chat is initiated, I added access to the GitHub repository and branch explicitly.
Action: When starting a new chat with a GEM, give it explicit access to all required repositories and ask it to reference the current state of the project.

Title: Rigorous L1 Diagram Audits
Discussion: The pre-flight audit of the Mermaid diagram successfully caught the misplaced SenseCap and NAS devices. Identifying this prevented a massive Zero-Trust violation before any logical IPs were assigned.
Action: Continue requiring explicit physical port mapping confirmations (via diagrams or lists) before executing any logical configuration.

Title: Boundary Validation via Failure
Discussion: The initial ICMP test failure (getting Destination Host Unreachable from 192.168.1.1) perfectly proved that the default-deny boundary from Feature 1.1 was functioning identically in practice as it did in theory.
Action: Formalize "expected failure" testing when working across logical boundaries to verify security postures.

Title: Peer-Review & Architectural Pushback
Discussion: You successfully caught my error regarding the 202-second resilience baseline. You correctly identified that the physical TL-SG108E switch maintains the cluster quorum, meaning the outage only affects WAN/Gateway access, not internal K8s eviction.
Action: Maintain this strict peer-review dynamic. We must continuously challenge each other's assumptions regarding blast radiuses and failure domains.

Title: Enforcing Agile Ceremonies
Discussion: We eagerly transitioned to Feature 1.3 planning the moment the DoD was met, completely bypassing the mandatory retrospective phase.
Action: Establish a hard stop at the end of every feature's execution. The AI must formally request the retrospective before generating the next pre-flight action plan.

Title: Anticipating Firmware Limitations
Discussion: We lost execution time attempting to delete an active DHCP lease because the ER605 standalone UI and Orbi AP mode hide standard network management menus.
Action: When dealing with consumer-grade or unmanaged hardware, default immediately to network-level workarounds (like the "DHCP Pool Squeeze") rather than relying on assumed UI toggles.

Title: GitOps State Assumptions
Discussion: I incorrectly assumed your Git repository was out of sync based on my limited static context window, generating a false Configuration Drift report.
Action: I must explicitly ask you to confirm your commit status (satisfying ABW) rather than assuming repository states I cannot dynamically query.
